text:
Joel Hofer stopped all 29 shots he saw at Delta Center, and the St. Louis Blues went home with a shootout win over Utah that their goalie, more than their skaters, made possible. Our numbers say the chances against him were worth 3.02 goals, so he saved about three more than an average goalie would have. Drafted 107th overall by the Blues in 2018 out of Swift Current, he was named first star in a game with no regulation goals at either end.

Utah had the better of the play. Our numbers give the Mammoth a 52 percent chance of winning the game if every shot were replayed (what we call deserved to win), and they led on shots on goal, 29 to 22, and on shot attempts, 63 to 58. The first period was theirs: they out-chanced St. Louis 1.18 to 0.39 in expected goals, a measure of shot quality, and Jack McBain had a 41 percent look that Hofer turned away. St. Louis grew into it, edging the second period and then owning the third, 1.11 to 0.59. Karel Vejmelka was just as sharp at the other end, stopping all 22 shots, worth 2.9 goals above expectation. Neither team scored on the power play (STL 0 for 5, UTA 0 for 4).

The shootout stayed tied through eight rounds. Connor McMichael, the No. 25 pick in 2019 from London, beat Vejmelka in the eighth, and Barrett Hayton was stopped to finish it. For Utah, it leaves the Mammoth winless in four (0-2-2), and a night of dominant chances produced one point at best.
